repairs.label: contract-fixture-owner
repairs.effect: The contract fixture owns a canonical migrated file database using the bounded runtime WAL factory, and uses a fresh real application that borrows this exact engine. It no longer replaces another cached application owner. The unchanged request helper and every original shape assertion remain intact. A real factory-owned cached-app control exposes one parent test identity with a call ownership failure and a teardown missing-table error after the borrowed in-memory catalog is disposed. Final control preserves the cached owner/canary, current SKU, right_panel across two requests, current Alembic heads, WAL and committed-only visibility during another transaction. Module control restores prior app owners, session factory and environment. Thirteen active combined contract/parity/cache-lifetime cases pass; two pre-existing shape placeholders remain skipped.
repairs.limits: Test fixture ownership/isolation repair, not a production application change or universal locking certificate. Original model/observer/audit-store exclusions for the shape profile are unchanged; image-match and security-block placeholders remain open. The historical source151full-process right_panel KeyError is preserved and not causally closed merely by these isolated passing controls. A later frozen broader process is still required. This cohort does not close the unadmitted-market or invented-image positive-authority gaps, distributed recovery or release/endurance qualification. Initial eight-pass/two-skip gate preceded stricter module-owner restoration and is superseded by the final13-pass/two-skip profile.

Two real private-SQL legacy-demo cases prove the persisted rows are unchanged. Exact parent11cases have6failures and5controls; all50combined projection/finalizer/stage/inventory/graph/fact checks pass without skips. The unchanged loader still classifies canonical facts partly by tenant, drops some provenance/validity data, lacks some future-time upper bounds and uses batch-wide status. Those gaps, licensing, aggregate privacy and useful cited buyer market analysis remain open. Controlled SQL rows are synthetic test inputs, not real market measurements. No application/browser source, actor permission, stored quantity or commercial authority changes. Earlier33-pass and15-pass profiles predate two additional zero-value controls and are superseded by the final50-case run. No final-source all-profile or release/endurance qualification.

repairs.label: model-transport-owner
repairs.effect: Coherently integrates authored role and gateway ownership handoff: a dispatched worker returns its per-model lease when transport actually finishes; gateway preflight/no-dispatch returns it immediately, and role request/gateway construction failure returns it without dispatch. Exact3 parent behavior checks have2 failures (premature timeout release and validation leak) and1 construction-fault control. Final41 active tests pass without skips, including11 new ownership/callback/current-execution controls,9 earlier deadline cases,5 supplier checks,4 real threaded scheduler checks,10 gateway controls and2 architecture boundary checks. Typed failures/current execution identity and fresh blocked-artifact schedule evidence are integrated and tested. Earlier unrelated working files remain byte-identical.
repairs.limits: A caller timeout or cancellation quarantines output rather than killing an arbitrary Python transport thread. A transport that never returns still owns its slot until process recovery; this patch prevents overlap and does not certify hard transport termination or distributed model scheduling. Concurrency is process-local, existing gate-key/maximum and gateway capacity remain unchanged, no live model/GPU/cloud or commercial provider was invoked. This final candidate excludes other authored runtime/router/CV/research changes. Full source151 observations remain historical and do not qualify this integration or a final release.
